title: An Exploration of How Volume Rendering is Impacted by Lossy Data Reduction
problem: Lossy data reduction is widely adopted for compressing scientific datasets to reduce storage overhead, but its impact on volume rendering visualization quality is poorly understood. The paper investigates which parameters (dataset characteristics, opacity, color) most significantly affect perception quality when lossy compression is applied.
motivation: Understanding the perceptual impact of data reduction on scientific visualization is essential as data reduction techniques become standard practice in large-scale simulations.
method: Conducts an in-depth empirical analysis of error-bound lossy data reduction techniques applied to volume rendering. Systematically examines how dataset characteristics, opacity, and color parameters affect the perception quality of rendered volumes across different compression levels.
key_novelty: First systematic study of how lossy compression techniques impact volume rendering perception quality, moving beyond theoretical compression metrics to study actual visual fidelity.
contributions: In-depth analysis framework for evaluating lossy compression impact on volume rendering quality
Empirical identification of dataset characteristics most affected by lossy compression
Understanding of how opacity and color parameters interact with lossy data reduction
Practical insights for selecting appropriate lossy reduction techniques for visualization

metrics.accuracy: visual quality and perceptual error relative to original uncompressed data

primary_theme: impact of lossy compression on volume rendering quality
